result: {"decisions":[{"item_type":"decision","point":"D2","problem":"Viral anecdotes of a model seeming to detect it is being tested do not show whether the ability is reliable.","did":"Built a benchmark with many tasks, questions and models to test whether situational awareness is systematic rather than a one-off.","alternatives_named":["isolated Twitter anecdotes","single-example demonstrations"],"stated_reason":"A larger evaluation shows whether an ability is systematic or just luck on a single question.","quote":"On Twitter, you often see impressive but isolated anecdotes. Our goal is more systematic evaluation. We have about 17 tasks with 12,000 questions, evaluating 19 different LLMs in various settings. This gives a much better picture of whether an ability is systematic or just luck on a single question."},{"item_type":"advice","point":"D5","problem":"Claude 3 Opus gave insightful answers on the long-form task, and these could be chance because sampling is random.","did":"Noted that sampling is at temperature 1 and treated the insights as real because they recurred often.","alternatives_named":["attributing the insights to luck"],"stated_reason":"The insights appeared often enough that luck is an unlikely explanation.","quote":"It’s worth noting we sample answers with temperature 1, so there’s some randomness. We saw these insights often enough that I don’t think it’s just luck."},{"item_type":"disagreement","point":"D5","problem":"GPT-4 base scored above zero on the long-form self-description task, which could be read as real self-knowledge.","did":"Favoured the deflationary reading that the questions resemble human-AI conversations, so the model is just doing next-token prediction.","alternatives_named":["GPT-4 base really knows at some level that it is an AI"],"stated_reason":"The questions are somehow typical of human-AI interactions rather than human-human ones.","quote":"I think it’s more likely the latter - the model is doing its normal thing. It doesn’t really have a deeper, more systematic situational awareness. Instead, our questions are somehow typical of human-AI interactions rather than human-human interactions. That’s my guess as to what’s going on."},{"item_type":"decision","point":"D6","problem":"Deciding whether to set a score threshold on the benchmark at which models count as dangerous.","did":"Declined to define a threshold and treated a high score only as one piece of evidence.","alternatives_named":["a clear danger threshold above which evaluations are no longer trusted"],"stated_reason":"Thresholds are hard to set because a cheap way of scoring well might exist without real practical situational awareness.","quote":"We did not create this dataset with some kind of clear threshold where if models score above it, they’re dangerous or we should stop trusting the evaluations. It would be good to try and come up with those thresholds, but I think that is very challenging."},{"item_type":"decision","point":"D1","problem":"Testing whether a model can follow instructions that conflict with its imitation-based training.","did":"Designed anti-imitation tasks where simply imitating training data leads to failure.","alternatives_named":["tasks solvable by imitating pre-training data"],"stated_reason":"Success then requires reading the instructions and suppressing the urge to imitate, as a deceptively aligned model would need to.","quote":"And so what we wanted is a case where if models just imitate examples of this task that are in its training data, then they will fail on the task."},{"item_type":"decision","point":"D1","problem":"Ruling out explanations for out-of-context reasoning, such as the need for a named latent variable.","did":"Included a mixture-of-functions task with no named latent variable to test that explanation, not to show scary capability.","alternatives_named":["naming the latent state or variable"],"stated_reason":"It rules out some theories about what is going on.","quote":"The mixture of functions is not intended to be scary or impressive. It’s more about ruling out some theories about what’s going on. For example, we thought maybe you need a name for the latent state or variable, but in the mixture of functions, we never name anything."},{"item_type":"advice","point":"D2","problem":"Judging whether a model can learn a harder latent structure out of context before scaling up.","did":"Recommends first checking whether the model can use the structure in context or after fine-tuning.","alternatives_named":["scaling up without checking in-context ability"],"stated_reason":"If the model cannot succeed even with fine-tuning, it probably will not manage the out-of-context version.","quote":"You can check if the models can do this kind of reasoning in context.
